question: What changes when Representation Contract is elevated from a methodological idea to a mandatory operational gate?
answer: JANUS no longer treats comparison as intrinsically interpretable. Comparison becomes conditional: a claim about invariant I is blocked unless the selected representation R has an explicit preservation contract relevant to I, plus a metric, reference frame, controls, falsifier, multiplicity rule, provenance, and explicit OPEN/NULL/BLOCKED handling.

key_upgrade.before: A difference could be measured first and justified later.
key_upgrade.after: Interpretive rights must be established before verdict. Exploratory measurement remains allowed but is explicitly non-authoritative until contract validation.

why_no_contract_is_not_fail: FAIL would imply the target claim was tested and lost. When no valid representation contract exists, the claim was not legitimately tested at all; therefore BLOCKED is the correct epistemic state.
why_97254_remains_canonical_calibration: The attractive SHA substring was not discarded when it failed prospectively and was not rescued by changing representation after the fact. It remains evidence about process discipline: exploratory observation may generate a test, but failed replication revokes confirmatory authority.
strongest_operational_law: CLAIM ABOUT I -> VALID REPRESENTATION CONTRACT FOR I -> METRIC -> CONTROL -> TEST -> VERDICT. Any skipped prerequisite removes interpretive authority from the downstream number.
canonical_seal: JANUS DOES NOT ASK ONLY WHETHER TWO THINGS DIFFER. JANUS FIRST ASKS WHETHER THE CHOSEN REPRESENTATION HAS THE RIGHT TO MAKE THAT DIFFERENCE MEAN ANYTHING ABOUT THE CLAIMED INVARIANT.
